howDoI.q: How do I make a key hop only once, however long it is held?
How do I make a key keep going while it is held down?
How do I let the hero rise above a tall cliff?
How do I make the hero dash?
How do I make a dash happen once for each press?
How do I size a gap so it needs a certain number of dashes?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Kit's Moves is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space hops, once for each press. Up lifts Kit for as long as it is held. Enter dashes to the right, once for each press. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Try each key tapped, and then held down. Nothing in this game can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: Tap and Hold
pages.html:
Level 1: Tap and Hold

SPACE HOPS ONCE PER PRESS. HOLD IT AND KIT STILL HOPS ONCE is the first sign. Hold Space as long as you like: Kit hops once and lands. Hop onto the low wall and take its coin. TOO TALL TO HOP. THE UP KEY IS DIFFERENT and HOLD UP. KIT KEEPS LIFTING WHILE THE KEY IS DOWN come next. Stand by the brick cliff and hold Up: Kit rises past the coins, and a tap lifts them only a little. When they are above the top, press Right, and walk to the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • One hop per press. Open hero.chr in the Character tab and look at the Space sequence. Its setting One sequence per key stroke is on, so when the frames run out the game goes back to standing, even while the key is held. A new press starts a new hop.
  • Keep going while held. The Up sequence has that setting off. When its frames run out and the key is still down, the game starts them again. Each frame pushes upward (it has the Momentum setting, so the push adds to their speed) and gravity takes it back, so while the key is held Kit climbs faster and faster, to a top speed.
  • Why a tap lifts a little. A short press runs only a few frames. The push is spent and gravity brings them down, so how far they go depends on how long the key was held.
  • The map. Open one.map: a wall three blocks high, which a hop clears, and a cliff nine blocks high with brick for its face and grass for the top. The coins beside the cliff are the ones you pass on the way up.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. A scene link joins the door at the right to the next level in km.gam.

pages.head: Level 2: Once Per Press
pages.html:
Level 2: Once Per Press

ENTER DASHES RIGHT, ONCE PER PRESS. HOLDING IT DASHES ONCE comes first. Hold Enter and Kit dashes about three blocks and then stops. Three gaps follow. The first is one block wide, and one dash clears it. A WIDER GAP. HOP, KEEP RIGHT HELD, PRESS ENTER is five blocks wide: a hop with Right held falls a little short, a hop with one dash in the air clears it. THE WIDEST GAP. HOP, KEEP RIGHT HELD, ENTER TWICE is seven blocks wide and needs a hop and two dashes, the second press right after the first dash ends. Take the coins and walk into the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The dash is a sequence. Open hero.chr and look at the sequence on the Enter key: six frames, each moving Kit right by 11 pixels. That is the most the engine lets them move in one tick, so a longer dash needs more frames, not bigger steps.
  • Once per press. One sequence per key stroke is on, so holding Enter does not start another dash. Cannot be interrupted is on too, so a dash always runs to its end, even if another key is pressed.
  • Sized by the map. Open two.map: the gaps are 1, 5 and 7 blocks wide. A dash is a little over three blocks and gravity does not wait for it, so one dash from the ground only clears the narrow gap. A hop with Right held carries Kit about four blocks, each dash in the air adds a little over three more (about two more than walking would), so the wider gaps need a hop and one dash, then a hop and two.
  • No harm in falling. A gap is only two blocks deep, with ground at the bottom, so Kit lands in it and can hop out. Nothing is lost.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. The last door links to the The End scene in km.gam.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot tell how long a key was held. A sequence only runs again while the key is down, or does not. A short tap and a long press are the same until the frames run out, so "hold longer to go higher" comes from repeating a push, not from measuring.
  • It cannot change speed in the middle of a sequence. Each frame has its own move, and that is all. A move is also capped at 11 pixels a tick.
  • One key runs one sequence at a time. Holding Right and Space together does not do both. A new key starts its sequence in place of the old one unless the old one cannot be interrupted.
  • A sequence has one key and one direction. A dash to the left is a sequence of its own, on its own key.
  • It cannot count presses for you. There is no cooldown or limit on dashes except what the level asks of the player.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Turn on One sequence per key stroke for Up, and watch the lift become a single push.
  • Turn it off for Space, then hold it: Kit hops again and again.
  • Add frames to the dash to make it longer, and the gaps wider to match.
  • Make a second dash sequence on another key that goes left.
  • Draw new frames for the lift, such as a spinning propeller on the beanie.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie has two levels to cross. One key hops once, however long you hold it, and another keeps lifting them while it is down. In the second, a dash goes once for each press, so a wide gap needs press after press. Signs say what each level shows, and the manual says how each is made.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
A held key can run again, or wait for the next press: it is one setting on a sequence
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Two short levels about what a key does while you hold it. Space hops once however long it is held, Up keeps lifting for as long as it is down, and Enter dashes once for each press. Each is a setting on a sequence in the character file, and the levels are built so that you feel the difference. Nothing here hurts. Signs explain each idea, and every level has a page on how it is made.

28.long: Dash to the right. One dash for each press: let go and press again for another.

57.long: Hop once. Holding the key does not hop again: it is one hop for each press.

72.long: Lift for as long as the key is held. Let go and Kit falls.

80.long: Move down. Nothing here to climb.
